The evidence is mostly one-sided: routine denial, impunity, and limited administrative action rather than genuine accountability.","evidence":[{"title":"2024 Country Reports on Human Rights Practices: Egypt","publisher":"U.S. Department of State via ecoi.net","date":"2025 annual report covering 2024","url":"https://www.ecoi.net/en/document/2128475.html","summary":"The report says the government in some cases reported investigations into torture/cruelty complaints that led to disciplinary measures against Interior Ministry employees in 1,217 incidents. That is direct evidence against accountability for security-force abuse.","question_ids":["2B.9","2B.5"]},{"title":"World Report 2024: Egypt","publisher":"Human Rights Watch","date":"2024","url":"https://www.hrw.org/world-report/2024/country-chapters/egypt","summary":"HRW reports that prosecutors refused a request to reopen the investigation into the forced disappearance, ill-treatment, and suspicious death in custody of economist Aymad Hadhoud. This is a denial and defensive justification, not an acceptance of responsibility for possible border-security failure.","question_ids":["2B.9","2B.5"]}]}
